title: Final time answer
description: Essential: The response must state the total time as 7.75 s (or equivalent).

title: Maximum acceleration phase
description: Important: The solution must correctly calculate the initial acceleration using maximum tension and weight (a = (120 N - mg)/m).

title: Velocity at tension limit
description: Important: The solution must find the velocity at the end of the acceleration phase using power and max tension (v_t = P_max / F_max = 10 m/s).

title: Constant power phase analysis
description: Important: The solution must apply the work-energy theorem or kinematics to relate power, displacement, and velocity change for the second phase.

title: Height split calculation
description: Important: The solution must correctly compute the height gained during the initial acceleration phase (h1 = v_t^2/(2a) = 10 m).

title: Steady-state velocity check
description: Optional: The solution may note the theoretical maximum speed at constant power (v_m = P_max/(mg) = 15 m/s) as a reference.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All calculations should maintain consistent SI units (kg, m, s, N, W).

title: Sign or force direction error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the net force for acceleration is incorrectly taken as (mg - F_max) or if gravity's direction is mishandled.

title: Power misuse
description: Pitfall: Penalize if power is incorrectly used as constant during the acceleration phase (P = F*v, but v changes) without justification.
